# Labelled STE corpus. Synthetic text, written for astack.
# A "# rule: <id>" line starts a section. "+ text" must make <id> fire, "- text" must not.
# "\n" in a case is a line break.

# rule: sentence-length
+ The importer reads each row from the file, checks the header, maps every column to a field, and writes the result to the staging table before the next batch starts.
+ The service keeps one connection pool for each region, and each pool holds ten connections that the workers share when the traffic in that region goes up at night.
+ When the user opens the settings page and changes the region, the app stores the new value, refreshes the token, and sends a request to the server for the new data.
+ The report that the team sends to the owner each Friday lists the open tickets, the merged pull requests, the failed builds and the plan for the next week of work.
+ Open the file that the hook reads from the plan, add one line for each phase and one line for each open question, then save the file.
+ Run the migration on the staging database first, compare the row counts with the production snapshot, and then run the same migration on the production database at night.
+ The cache in front of the search service holds the results of the last thousand queries, and it drops the oldest result when a new query comes in after the limit.
+ The parser that reads the configuration file accepts comments, blank lines and quoted values, but it rejects tabs at the start of a line and keys that have no value.
+ Before you merge the branch, rebase it on the main branch, run every test in the repo, read the diff once more, and ask the owner for a review of the change.
+ The new endpoint returns a page of results with a cursor, and the client sends that cursor back in the next request until the server returns an empty page to it.
+ Each worker in the pool takes one job from the queue, runs it with a timeout of thirty seconds, and writes the result or the error to the job table when it stops.
+ The script that builds the release notes reads every merged pull request since the last tag, groups them by label, and writes one section for each label in the output file.
+ The team agreed to keep the old API for one more quarter because two large clients still call it every day and they need time to move to the new version.
+ If the build fails on the main branch, stop every merge, find the commit that broke the build, revert it, and tell the author in the team channel about the revert.
+ The dashboard shows the number of active users, the number of failed jobs and the average response time for each service in the last hour, and it refreshes every minute.
+ The import job that runs every night at two in the morning reads the files from the bucket, checks each file against the schema, and moves the bad files to a separate folder.
+ The design keeps the state in the plan, the tracker and git, so a new session can start from any of them without the transcript of the old session or any notes.
+ Write the summary in the first paragraph of the pull request, list the changes in the second paragraph, and put the test results with their counts in the last paragraph.
+ The owner reads the plan on Monday morning, marks the steps that need a decision, and sends the questions back to the agent before the first session of the week starts.
+ The billing service sends one invoice for each team at the end of the month, and it adds a line for each seat that was active for more than one day in that month.
+ The mobile app keeps a local copy of the last fifty messages for each chat, so the user can read them without a network connection when the phone is in a tunnel.
+ Copy the template into the new folder, rename each file to match the module name, replace the placeholder text in every file, and commit the result as the first commit of the branch.
+ The audit log records each change to a role with the time, the actor, the old value and the new value, and the security team reviews that log once a week.
+ The search page sends the query to the server after the user stops typing for three hundred milliseconds, so the server does not get a request for every single key press.
+ The release checklist asks the owner to confirm the version number, the changelog entry, the migration status and the feature flags before the team tags the release on the main branch.
+ The queue keeps failed jobs for seven days so that the team can read the error, fix the cause in the code, and run the same job again from the admin page.
+ Delete the old index only after the new index has served every query for one full week, and keep a snapshot of the old index in cold storage for one more month after that.
+ The test suite runs the unit tests first because they take less than a minute, and it runs the slow integration tests only when every unit test passes on that commit.
+ The export that the finance team runs at the end of each quarter reads every invoice, converts each amount to one currency, and writes one row for each customer in the file.
+ Make sure that the staging environment uses the same version of the database as production, the same feature flags, and a copy of the production data from the last night.
+ The first draft of the document had six sections, but the team cut it to three sections after the review because the other sections repeated facts from the design document.
